maria (eng-security): FYI we received a DSAR from an EU user requesting deletion of embeddings + backups. they attached govt ID.
jon (privacy): thanks. do we have the S3 prefix and key namespace? any replicas?
maria (eng-security): yes: s3://redwood-embeddings/eu/customer-7890/ encrypted with kms:alias/rdw-eu-emb. nightly snapshot copies exist in us-west-2 via replication.
lee (eng-platform): replication uses different CMK ARNs in each region. deletion needs to ensure replica objects are removed and any kms grants revoked; don't schedule CMK deletion.
sara (legal): confirm whether legal hold applies. requester included notarized proof so privacy can request erase after validation.
jon (privacy): i'll validate identity now. what's the proposed erase workflow that preserves auditability and supports vuln triage if needed?
maria (eng-security): proposed steps:
  1) create ephemeral service account dsar-runner with narrow perms (s3:ListBucket, s3:DeleteObject on prefix; kms:Decrypt/Describe on CMKs only). TTL 1h.
  2) mark snapshot metadata as "erasure-in-progress" in snapshot-service so restores skip it.
  3) run deletion: remove live objects in eu, then call snapshot-service to delete snapshots and instruct replica-region agent to remove replicas.
  4) revoke KMS grants for any service principals that had access to those objects. rotate data keys if necessary.
  5) produce audit package: object list (keys + sha256), KMS key IDs, deletion ops log with signed timestamp envelope. redact unrelated PII. upload to evidence vault and send receipt to requester.
lee (eng-platform): RBAC nuance: privacy team should not get S3/KMS permissions. instead create workflow role privacy.erase_requester which can trigger the dsar-run job token. that'll provide separation of duty.
jon (privacy): good. legal wants a proof package including signed event envelope and key ARNs. also want revocation evidence for grants.
maria (eng-security): audit service will include grant revocation records and KMS `RevokeGrant` traces. we only include object metadata hashes, not raw embedding vectors (data minimization).
sara (legal): ensure manifests are scrubbed for any other customers. approved to proceed assuming identity verified.
ops-bot: Runbook invoked: runbook/dsar/erase-procedure v3 by maria
jon (privacy): are there timeline estimates? we need quick turnaround but also need to ensure cross-region deletes propagate.
maria (eng-security): estimate: EU live deletion ~30m. replica GC ~up to 8h depending on replication lag. snapshot-service reports will be polled.
lee (eng-platform): implementation detail: for us-west-2 replica deletion we'll call regional agent with a signed workflow token to avoid giving global rights. also will add observability alert to watch for snapshot-service error spikes.
maria (eng-security): internal commands (redacted):
```
# mark snapshot as erasing
curl -X POST "https://internal.redwood/snapshot/v1/mark" -H "Authorization: Bearer $WF_TOKEN" -d '{"snapshot_id":"snap-20250402-7890","status":"erasure_in_progress","initiator":"maria"}'
# delete objects
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-embeddings/eu/customer-7890/ --recursive --region eu-west-1
```
jon (privacy): please capture KMS grant revocations in the audit bundle. also include the workflow token id and TTL.
maria (eng-security): will capture. adding two-person approval requirement (privacy + eng-security) to start the live erase. token TTL 30m.
sara (legal): approved. hold if any subpoena or retention exception found during process. notify legal immediately.
ops-bot: Approval recorded: 2-person check passed. job queued.
maria (eng-security): update: live EU objects removed at 4509871405. snapshot-service reports replica-delete queued for us-west-2.
lee (eng-platform): seeing replica delete queued; replication lag ~6m.
maria (eng-security): final: us-west-2 replicas removed, KMS grants revoked, audit package uploaded (evidence-id: ev-4509871235). sending receipt to requester.
jon (privacy): received. adding closure note.
sara (legal): reviewed. no retention exception needed. closing ticket.
